question: On 26 March, Stefano Rebora, President of the NGO Music for Peace, was arbitrarily denied entry and expelled by the Egyptian authorities at Cairo airport, where he had travelled in order to then oversee the consignment of 60 tonnes of humanitarian aid (mainly medicines) destined for the Gaza Strip. Rebora was taken behind closed doors and deprived of his personal effects and mobile phone.

Later – and only after the intervention of a few politicians whom he had managed to call immediately after his detention – he was led back to arrivals. In the end, he was expelled and repatriated on a flight to Italy on the official grounds of ‘serious national security concerns’. This is only the latest in a series of serious repressive acts that Egypt has waged against Rebora from Music for Peace and other NGOs.
Before this, in 2018 – despite the ambassador stepping in – Egypt denied Rebora entry for the first time, providing no justification. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Vice-President / High Representative (VP/HR) aware of the way in which the Egyptian authorities have treated Stefano Rebora, without providing justification?
What action does the VP/HR intend to take to end repressive action like this and see to it that Stefano Rebora is granted entry to Egypt?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.5.2024) The European External Action Service (EEAS) was informed about this case by the EU Delegation to Egypt after liaising with Italian authorities. While Member States remain competent to provide consular protection to their own nationals, the EEAS and in particular the EU Delegation to Egypt remain available to provide, within their remit and mandate, support to Italian authorities in dealing with the present case upon their request.
